Case 01 · Belgrade, Serbia
Brand meets heritage
BIGZ Building — State Printing House, 1937 · 2,690 m²
Translate a tech brand into a 1937 industrial landmark — without losing either story.

Solution: used the architecture as the narrative. High ceilings, sculptural ceiling forms, micro-cement, and industrial lighting made the heritage visible. Activity-based zoning — lounges, call pods, booth seats, communal tables — made the brand liveable.
Case 02 · Tbilisi, Georgia
Finding the brand from scratch
New physical identity · 2024
A residential building converted to office, low ceilings, reused furniture from a closed office — and a brand new identity no one knew how to translate into physical space.

Solution: pushed an experimental concept through tight constraints — limited revisions, local contractors unused to this kind of brief. The wave ceiling installation, iridescent panels, and chromatic palette gave the brand its first spatial language. Every detail was negotiated and fought for.
Case 03 · Poland
Reinventing how a HQ works
European HQ · 8,000 m²
8,000 m² European HQ. The most anticipated office project in the region — built for engineers, clients, and senior leadership alike.

The local management came in with one vision for the office. They left with something better. A space that shifted how the entire team thinks about coming to work — and proved that the right environment changes more than just the interior.
